name: Mobility Fundamentals
summary: Daily-ready mobility for calisthenics: wrists, shoulder flexion/extension, pike/pancake, bridge. Run before skill work.

goal.notes: Pass all mobility checkpoints — pain-free ROM for planche/handstand/lever prep

programming.notes: 5–15 min sessions. Never force end-range. Breathe through holds.

safety.notes: Mobility is conditioning — mild stretch discomfort ok; sharp pain is not.

divergence_notes: GMB/FF emphasize daily wrist + shoulder prep; pancake/bridge depth varies widely by anatomy.

timeline.from_level: Pain-free daily movement, forward fold to shins
timeline.human_label: 6–13 months of near-daily short sessions to own all three tracks
timeline.notes: No controlled trial gives time-to-range for these positions, so every step here is `estimated`. The one sourced anchor is the connective-tissue window: loaded tissue takes at least 8 weeks to change stiffness and ≥12 weeks to do so reliably (bohm-2015-tendon), which sets the floor on the loaded wrist and bridge steps. Range work responds to frequency far more than to session length.

prerequisite_standards.name: No acute joint pain in daily movement
prerequisite_standards.rationale: Range work on an irritated joint reliably makes it worse.

prerequisite_standards.name: Forward fold
prerequisite_standards.rationale: Baseline posterior-chain length before loaded compression work.

plateau_signatures.signal: Range improves within a session but resets by the next one, for weeks on end
typical_causes: Passive stretching without any loaded or active work at end range
Practising twice a week rather than near-daily
resolution: Add loaded end-range holds and active lifts out of the stretch
Shorten sessions and raise frequency toward daily

plateau_signatures.signal: No change over 6+ months of consistent, well-executed practice
typical_causes: Hip socket geometry — a genuine structural limit that training does not change
resolution: Reassess whether the skills you want actually require this range
Route around it: a wider straddle is not required for most trees

injury_risk_timeline.mechanism: Extension loaded through the lumbar spine when thoracic and shoulder range are insufficient
prophylaxis: Earn mob-shoulder-flexion before full bridge work
Push the floor away to shift extension into the thoracic spine
Stop at the point where the ribs flare
red_flags: Localised lumbar pinching at the top of the bridge
Post-session lower-back stiffness lasting into the next day

productive.notes: The one tree where near-daily short exposure clearly beats fewer hard sessions. Keep sessions to 10–20 minutes.

too_much_signals: Joint ache rather than muscular stretch sensation
Range worse the day after a session
Needing to warm up longer to reach yesterday's position

deload.protocol: Keep frequency, drop to unloaded range only for one week.
deload.trigger: Joint irritation, or six weeks without range change.
